source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 4. Exercises reused from the lesson.

title.en: Iman — the faith of a Muslim

topic: Faith is light, doubt is darkness; the six pillars of iman

learn.en: Iman is an Arabic word. It means faith: complete trust, believing with all your heart without any doubt.
learn.title: Iman means faith

learn.en: Doubt and faith are opposites. Faith is light; doubt is darkness.
learn.title: Light and darkness

learn.en: With iman the heart accepts the truth, the tongue says it, and the limbs act on it.
learn.title: Heart, tongue and actions

learn.en: A Muslim believes in: Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Day of Judgement, and Divine Destiny — that everything good or bad comes from Allah.
learn.title: The six pillars of iman

learn.en: “All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers.” (Qur'an 2:285)
learn.title: From the Qur'an

order.en: Put the six pillars of iman in order

quiz.en: Which of these is NOT one of the six pillars of iman?
True or false? A Muslim believes that everything good or bad comes from Allah.

think.q: Can you count the six things a Muslim believes in on your fingers?
think.a: Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, and Divine Destiny!

parents.summary: Iman = faith with no doubt, in the heart, on the tongue and in actions; its six pillars: Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, Divine Destiny.
parents.tip: Count the six pillars of iman on his fingers together.
